Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words, ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾, that he said: This covers that, and that covers this.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words, ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾, that he said: He brings in the day and takes away the night, and brings in the night and takes away the day.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾: when He takes away the night and wraps the day over it, and takes away the day and wraps the night over it.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾:

He, exalted is His mention, says: He subjected the sun and the moon to His servants, so that by them they may know the number of years and the reckoning, and distinguish the night from the day for the benefit of their livelihood. ﴿Each runs for a specified term﴾: he says, ﴿each﴾ of them, meaning the sun and the moon, ﴿runs for a specified term﴾, meaning until the Hour arrives, and that is until the sun is wound up and the stars fall. It was also said: the meaning of that is that each of the two has stations which it neither exceeds nor falls short of. ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾: He, exalted is His mention, says: Unquestionably, Allah, who did these deeds and bestowed these blessings upon His creation, is the Mighty in His retribution against those who opposed Him, the Forgiving of the sins of His servants who turn to Him in repentance from them, by His pardoning them for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 6:

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no god but He. So how are you turned away?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿He created you﴾, O people, ﴿from a single soul﴾, meaning from Adam, ﴿then made from it its mate﴾, meaning: then made from Adam his spouse Eve, and that is because Allah created her from one of his ribs.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said in accordance with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam, then He created from him his mate Eve, creating her from one of his ribs.

If someone says: How is it said, "He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate," when the children of Adam were created from Adam and his wife, and there is no doubt that the parents precede the child? There are several answers to this. The first is that it may be said: this was said because it was reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back, and brought forth every soul that would exist until the Day of Resurrection. Then He settled him in the Garden after that, and after that created Eve from a rib of his ribs." This is one view. The second: the Arabs sometimes report about a man two actions, and the first of them is mentioned in meaning with "then" (thumma) when it is from the speech of the speaker, as one says: "What you did today has reached me, then what you did yesterday is more amazing," so this is a sequence from the speaker's report. The other view: that his creating the mate is referred back to its singular, as if it were said: He created you from a soul alone, then made from it its mate, so that in "wahida" (single) there is the meaning "He created her alone." As the rajaz poet said:

I have prepared him for the adversary who transgresses... you overcame him from you without effort.

[The two verses are rajaz, cited by the author of Lisan al-'Arab under "kawwaha" as evidence that its kawh means turning back. Al-Azhari said: al-taksih is domination, and Abu 'Amr recited: "I prepared him for the adversary..." It is also among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 283), where he said, interpreting His saying "He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate": is the spouse created before the offspring? There are two points of Arabic on this. One is that when the Arabs report about a man two actions, they refer the latter with "then" if it is the latter in meaning, and they sometimes make "then" carry the meaning of priority, using "then" in the speaker's report. Among that: you say, "What you did this day has reached me, then what you did yesterday is more amazing," so this is a sequence from the speaker's report; and you say, "I gave you something today, then what I gave you yesterday is more." The other view is to make the creation of the spouse referred back to "wahida," as if he said: He created you from a soul alone, then made from it its mate, so that in "wahida" there is the meaning of its being created alone. He said: some Arabs recited to me: "I prepared him for the adversary..." and its meaning: he who, when he transgresses, I overcome; and kawwahtuhu: I overcame him.]

That is, "the one who, if he transgresses, I overcome him"; and "kawwahtuhu" means "I overcame him."

The view that the people of knowledge hold is more correct, and it is the first view I mentioned: that Allah brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins before He created Eve. Reports to this effect have come from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The other two views are according to the schools of the Arabic linguists.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock eight pairs﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He made for you of the livestock eight mates: two of camels, two of cattle, two of sheep, and two of goats, as He, may His praise be glorified, said: ﴿eight pairs: two of the sheep and two of the goats﴾.

As:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿of the livestock eight pairs﴾: "Of the camels, cattle, sheep and goats."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock eight pairs﴾: two of camels, two of cattle, two of sheep, two of goats, a pair from each kind.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you of the livestock eight pairs﴾: meaning two of goats, two of sheep, two of cattle, two of camels.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He begins your creation, O people, in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation; that is, He causes a drop (nutfah) to form in it, then makes it a clinging clot ('alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah), then bones, then clothes the bones with flesh, then brings it forth as another creation, blessed be Allah, exalted is He. That is His creating it, creation after creation.

As:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾: a drop, then a clot, then a lump.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿creation after creation﴾: a drop, then what follows it until its creation is complete.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾: a drop, then a clot, then a lump, then bones, then flesh, then hair grew; stages of creation.

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾: he said: meaning creation after creation: a clot, then a lump, then bones.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾: they become drops, then they become clots, then they become lumps, then they become bones, then the spirit is breathed into them.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾: a creation of a drop, then a clot, then a lump.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: He creates you in the wombs of your mothers after His creating you in the loins of Adam. They said: that is the creation after the creation.

Those who said this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾: a creation in the wombs after the first creation in which He created them in the loins of Adam.

The most correct of the two views on this is the view said by 'Ikrimah and Mujahid, and whoever says the like of their view, because Allah, mighty and majestic, informed that He creates us, creation after creation, in the wombs of our mothers, in three darknesses, and He did not inform that He creates us in the wombs of our mothers after our creation in the loins of Adam. This is like His saying: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay, then We made him a drop in a firm place, then We made the drop a clot...﴾ to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾

It means: the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta (mashimah).

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: the three darknesses are: the belly, the womb, and the placenta.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: the belly, the placenta, and the womb.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: he said: by the three darknesses is meant: the belly of his mother, the womb, and the placenta.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: the belly, the womb, and the placenta.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: the placenta, the womb, and the belly.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: he said: the darkness of the placenta, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the belly.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: the placenta is within the womb, and the womb is within the belly.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾: the womb, the placenta, and the belly; and the placenta is that which is upon the child when it comes out, and it is among animals the afterbirth (al-saliy).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This One who did these deeds, O people, is your Lord, not one who cannot bring benefit to himself, nor ward off harm from himself, nor bring you good, nor ward off evil from you, from your idols and your gods.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to Him belongs the dominion﴾

He, mighty and majestic, says: To your Lord, O people, whose attributes are what He described to you, and whose power is what He made clear to you, belongs the dominion, the dominion of this world and the next and their authority, not to another. As for the kings of this world, each one possesses something to the exclusion of other things, so he has only a particular share of dominion. But the complete dominion, which is dominion in the absolute sense, belongs to Allah, the One, the Subduer.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There is no god but He. So how are you turned away?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: No one should be worshipped besides Him, and worship is fitting only for Him. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So how are you turned away, O people, and go away from worshipping your Lord, who has this description, to worshipping one who has no harm or benefit for you?

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah (﴿fa-anna tusrafun﴾): he said: like His saying: ﴿tu'fakun﴾.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾: he said to the polytheists: how are your minds turned away from this?

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of the contents of the breasts.﴾ (39:7)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding His words: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief.﴾ Some of them said: this is specific to a particular group of people, and its meaning is: If you disbelieve, O polytheists, in Allah, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants, the believers whom He has chosen sincerely for His worship and obedience, disbelief. * Mention of those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief.﴾ He means the disbelievers whose hearts Allah did not intend to purify, so that they would say: "There is no god but Allah." Then He said: ﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾, and they are His sincere servants about whom He said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾, so He obligated them to the testimony that there is no god but Allah and made it beloved to them.

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ He said: He does not approve for His believing servants that they disbelieve.

Others said: rather, this is general to all people, and its meaning is: O people, if you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you, and He does not approve for you that you disbelieve in Him.

The correct view on this matter is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: If you disbelieve in Allah, O disbelievers, then indeed Allah is Free of need of your faith and your worship of Him, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief, meaning: He does not approve for His servants that they disbelieve in Him, as one says: "I do not love injustice, and if you wish that so-and-so wrong so-and-so, then he will be punished."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾

It means: And if you believe in your Lord and obey Him, He approves your gratitude to Him, and that is their belief in Him and their obedience to Him. Gratitude is alluded to without being mentioned, and only the verb indicating it is mentioned, and this is similar to His words: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them," and it increased them in faith﴾, meaning: the saying of the people to them increased them in faith.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ He said: If you obey, He approves it for you.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾

It means: No sinner bears the sin of another sinner besides her, and she is not held accountable except for the sin of her own self. He, Mighty and Majestic, informs His servants that upon every soul is what it has earned, and that it is not held accountable for the sin of another.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ He said: No one is taken for the sin of anyone.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾

The One mentioned says, exalted is His remembrance: Then, after you have committed in this world what you have committed of good and evil, and faith and disbelief, O people, your return is to your Lord after your death. ﴿And He will inform you﴾ means: He will tell you of what you used to do in this world of good and evil, and will recompense you for all of that, the doer of good by his goodness and the doer of evil by what he deserves. He, Mighty and Majestic, says to His servants: Beware of meeting your Lord having done in this world what He does not approve of from you, and thus perishing, for no deed of any doer among you is hidden from Him.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of the contents of the breasts﴾

The One mentioned says, exalted is His remembrance: Indeed Allah is not concealed from anything that your breasts, O people, conceal, which your eyes cannot perceive, so how much more so what the eyes perceive and the sights see. What is meant by this, Mighty and Majestic, is the report that nothing is hidden from Him, and that He takes account of His servants' deeds so that He may recompense them for them, that they might fear Him in the secrets of their affairs and in their open matters.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 8:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before, and sets up rivals to Allah, to mislead [others] from His way. Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."﴾ (39:8)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And when harm touches man" means: when affliction in his body touches him, whether from illness, or a calamity, or hardship in his livelihood, and exertion and distress, ﴿he calls upon his Lord﴾, meaning: he seeks help from his Lord, who created him, because of the severity of that, and he turns to Him, desiring the removal of the hardship that has befallen him.

* *

His saying: ﴿turning to Him in repentance﴾

means: repentant to Him from what he had been upon before that, of disbelief in Him and associating the gods and idols with Him in worship, returning to His obedience.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man﴾ — he said: the pain, the affliction and the hardship. ﴿He calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾ — he said: seeking help from Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself﴾

His exalted remembrance means: then when his Lord grants him a favor from Himself, meaning well-being, so He removes his harm, and replaces his sickness with health, and his hardship with ease.

The Arabs say of everyone who gives another wealth or other things: "He has khawwalahu (bestowed upon him)." From it is the saying of Abu al-Najm al-'Ijli:

He gave and did not withhold, and was not made to withhold... the high-humped camels from the possessions of the one who bestows.

[The verse is by Abu al-Najm al-'Ijli, the well-known rajaz poet (Lisan: kh-w-l). He praises a man who gave those who asked him fat camels high of hump; "al-dhura" is the plural of "dhirwa," the highest part of a thing. These were among what God had bestowed upon him and granted him, and his giving was abundant, so he did not withhold it, and no one attributed stinginess to him. The verse is among the evidences of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (p. 216), at His saying: "Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself": every possession of yours, and everything you have given, you have khawwaltahu; Abu al-Najm said: "He gave and did not withhold..."]

* And Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna Abu 'Ubaydah narrated to me that he said: I heard Abu 'Amr say, concerning the verse of Zuhayr:

There, if they are asked for wealth, they bestow it, and if they are asked, they give, and if they gamble, they wager high.

[The verse is by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma al-Muzani (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the explanation of Mustafa al-Saqqa, p. 239). The narration in it is "yastakhlibu" in place of "yastakhwalu." In the Lisan it says: "al-istikhwal" is also like "al-istikhbal," from akhbaltuhu al-mal: when I lent him a she-camel to benefit from its milk and wool, or a horse to raid upon. From it is Zuhayr's saying: "There, if they seek to be lent wealth... the verse." The meaning of "yayassiru" is: they gamble. "Yaghulu": they choose the fat camels at a high price and gamble over them. The verse is among the evidences of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (216b), where he said: I heard Abu 'Amr say concerning Zuhayr's verse "There... etc.": Yunus said: we only heard it as "There, if they seek to be lent the wealth (yastakhlibu)," meaning they lend (yakhbilu), and it has the same meaning.]

Ma'mar said: Yunus said: we only heard it as:

There, if they seek to be lent camels, they lend them.

He said: and it has the same meaning.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself﴾: when well-being or good befalls him.

* *

His saying: ﴿he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before﴾

means: he abandons his supplication which he had been directing to God before He removed the harm he had been suffering. ﴿And sets up rivals to Allah﴾ means: partners.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿he forgot﴾, he said: he abandoned; this is specifically about the disbeliever.

As for the "ma" in His saying ﴿he forgets what he had been﴾, there are two possibilities. The first: that it means "alladhi" (that which), and the meaning of the statement then is: he abandoned the one he had been calling upon in the state of the harm he was in, meaning by it God, may His remembrance be exalted; so "ma" is in that case placed in the position of "man" (who), as it is said: ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾, meaning God, and as it is said: ﴿so marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [4:3]. The second: that it means the infinitive (masdar), as I have mentioned. When it is the infinitive, the pronoun in His saying ﴿to Him﴾ has two possibilities: the first, that it refers back to "ma"; the second, that it refers back to the Lord.

* *

His saying: ﴿and sets up rivals to Allah﴾

means: and makes for Allah likenesses and equals.

Then the people of interpretation differed about the sense in which they made them rivals to Him. Some of them said: they made them rivals to Him in obeying them in disobedience to God.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and sets up rivals to Allah﴾: he said: the rivals among men, whom they obey in disobedience to God.

Others said: it means that he worshipped idols, so he made them rivals to Allah in worshipping them.

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this is the statement of the one who said: it means that he obeyed Satan in worshipping idols, so the idols became rivals for him, because that is within the context of God's rebuke to them for worshipping them.

* *

His saying: ﴿to mislead [others] from His way﴾

means: to remove from the path of God whoever wished to make Him one and believe in Him, from His unity, and acknowledgment of Him, and entering Islam.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little"﴾

means: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to the one who does that: enjoy your disbelief in God for a little, until you fulfill your term, and your death comes to you, ﴿indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire﴾: meaning, indeed you are among the people of the Fire, who will remain in it forever.

* *

His saying: ﴿Enjoy your disbelief﴾

is a threat and warning from God.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only the people of understanding are reminded.﴾ (39:9)

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words: ﴿أَمِنَ﴾ (ʾamman). Some Meccan and some Medinan reciters, and the majority of the Kufans, recited it as "Amman" with the mim lightened (ʾamman, with a single m). For their recitation in this form there are two possible meanings. The first is that the alif in "Amman" carries the sense of a vocative (du'a'), meaning: "O you who are devoutly obedient during the hours of the night." The Arabs address with the alif just as they address with yā, so they say, "Azid aqbil" and "Yā Zaid aqbil" (both meaning "Zayd, come forward"). Among this usage is the verse of Aws ibn Hajar:

Abanī Lubaynā, lastum bi-yadin ... illā yadun laysat lahā ʿadud
[[The verse has already been cited in volume 14 (p. 110) and explained at length there, so refer back to it. The verse is also one of al-Farra's witnesses in Maʿani al-Qurʾan (folio 284), and the point of citing it here is that the Arabs call with the hamza just as they call with yā. Al-Farra said: regarding the words of Him, the Exalted, "Amman huwa qanitun ana' al-layl," Yahya ibn Wathhab recited it with the lightened form, and this is also transmitted from Nafi' and Hamza, and they explained it as meaning "O you who are devoutly obedient," which is a good reading. The Arabs address with an alif just as they address with yā, saying "Yā Zayd aqbil" and "Azid aqbil." A poet said, "Abanī Lubaynā..." and another said, "Aḍmir ibn Ḍamrah..." This is common in poetry. The meaning then is that the verse is connected to what precedes by way of address, like a parallel. For He mentioned the forgetful disbeliever and then related the account of the righteous one by way of address, as you would say in speech: "So-and-so does not pray or fast," then "O you who prays and fasts, rejoice!" This is its meaning. The alif may also be interrogative, with the sense of "am" (or), since the Arabs sometimes place "am" in the position of the alif when a statement has preceded it; and I have described from this what suffices, so the meaning is "Is the one who is devoutly obedient...?" like the first one who was mentioned with forgetfulness and disbelief. Whoever reads it with the shadda (doubled m) intends the meaning of the alif, which is the correct sense: "am" is placed when it is a response to a meaning that has already gone before. Al-Hasan, ʿAsim and Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani recited it this way, meaning "am man huwa." It is clear in the speech that there is an implied element whose meaning was already expressed at the beginning of the word, since He mentioned the astray one and then mentioned the guided one by way of interrogation, which is evidence that the meaning is: "Is this like that?" or "Is this better?" Whoever does not know the ways of the Arabs, and does not perceive the meaning in this and similar cases, will not be satisfied or healed.]]

If the alif is taken as a vocative, the meaning of the speech is: "Say: Enjoy your disbelief a little, for you are among the companions of the Fire; and O you who are devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, you are among the people of Paradise." The Fire is a blindness for the disbelieving group concerning the recompense of God in the Hereafter, and this suffices as an explanation of what belongs to the believing group, since the difference in their conditions in this world is known, and it is understood that if one of them is among the companions of the Fire because of his disbelief in his Lord, the other is among the companions of Paradise. So the predicate concerning the latter is omitted, relying on the hearer's understanding of what is meant from its mention, since the omitted part has been indicated by what is stated.

The second possibility is that the alif in His words "Amman" is an interrogative alif, so the meaning of the speech is: "Is this like the one who set up rivals to God so as to lead astray from His way?" And He is satisfied with what has already preceded of God's report concerning the group of disbelief in Him among His enemies, since the intended meaning of the speech is understood, as the poet said:

Fa-uqsimu law shayʾun atānā rasūluhu ... siwāka wa-lākin lam najid laka madfaʿā
[[The verse has already been cited and explained at length in volume 12 (p. 18), so refer back there. Al-Farra also cited it in Maʿani al-Qurʾan (folio 284) after the passage I transmitted from him under the previous witness, saying: Do you not see the poet's words, "Fa-uqsimu law shayʾun atānā rasūluhu..." that its meaning is: "If a messenger other than you had come to us, we would have repelled him," so the meaning is known though it is not stated. His words "Afaman sharaḥa Allāhu ṣadrahu lil-Islām" follow this same pattern.]]

So the omission of "lo daf'anāhu" (we would have repelled him) is intended in the speech, since its meaning was understood by the hearer.

Some reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited it as "Ammman" with the mim doubled, meaning "am man huwa?" They say that it is an interrogative "ammān" introduced into the speech after a statement that had already passed, so they brought "am." On this interpretation the answer to the interrogative must be left out, because the report concerning the group of disbelief and what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter has already been given, and then the report concerning the group of faith followed, so the meaning is known and the hearer's understanding of the meaning from the mention is sufficient, since it is understood that the meaning is: "Is this better, or is that?"

Our view on this is that both are readings, each recited by scholars among the reciters, and both are sound in interpretation and in grammatical analysis; whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

We have already mentioned the differences of those who differ, and the correct statement in our view regarding the meaning of "qānit" was given earlier, enough that it need not be repeated here. However, we mention here some of what the people of interpretation have said on this point, so that the reader of this book may know the agreement of this meaning in this place and elsewhere. Some of them said that in this place it means the one who recites the Qur'an standing in prayer.

Those who said so:

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya related to us from ʿUbaydullah, who said: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn ʿUmar, that when he was asked about qunut, he said: "I know of qunut only as the recitation of the Qur'an and the prolonged standing," and he recited: "Amman huwa qānitun ānāʾ al-layl sājidan wa-qāʾiman."

Others said that it means obedience.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, my uncle related to me, my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words "Amman huwa qānit": he meant by qunut obedience, because He said: "Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you will come forth" ... up to "Every one is devoutly obedient to Him" (qānitūn), and he said: "obedient."
- Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words "Amman huwa qānitun ānāʾ al-layl sājidan wa-qāʾiman": he said: the qānit is the obedient one.

And His words: ﴿ānāʾ al-layl﴾ (during the hours of the night)

He means: the hours of the night.

As:
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "Amman huwa qānitun ānāʾ al-layl": at its beginning, its middle and its end.
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, "ānāʾ al-layl": he said: the hours of the night.

Our explanation of the meaning of "ānāʾ" has already passed, with its evidence and the reports of the people of interpretation on it, enough that it need not be repeated here.

And His words: ﴿sājidan wa-qāʾiman﴾ (prostrating and standing)

He says: he is devoutly obedient, prostrating at times and standing at times, meaning he obeys. In our view qunut is obedience, and for this reason "sājidan wa-qāʾiman" is in the accusative, because its meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating at one time and standing at another?" So both are circumstantial accusatives (ḥāl) of "qānit."

And His words: ﴿yaḥdharu al-ākhirah﴾ (fearing the Hereafter)

He says: he fears the punishment of the Hereafter.

As:
- ʿAli ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi related to us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Yaman related to us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words "yaḥdharu al-ākhirah": he said: he fears the punishment of the Hereafter, and hopes for the mercy of his Lord, meaning he hopes that God will have mercy on him and admit him into Paradise.

And His words: ﴿Qul hal yastawī alladhīna yaʿlamūna wa-alladhīna lā yaʿlamūn﴾ (Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?)

He, the Exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to your people: Are those who know what they have for their obedience to their Lord of reward, and what they incur for their disobedience of Him of consequences, equal to those who do not know that, who wander blindly, neither hoping for good from their good deeds nor fearing evil from their bad ones? He means: these two are not equal.

It has been transmitted from Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli concerning this:
- Muhammad ibn Khalaf related to me, saying: Nasr ibn Muzahim related to me, saying: Sufyan al-Jurayri related to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi Mujahid, from Jabir, from Abu Jaʿfar, may God be pleased with him, regarding "Hal yastawī alladhīna yaʿlamūna wa-alladhīna lā yaʿlamūn": he said: "We are those who know, and our enemies are those who do not know."

And His words: ﴿Innamā yatadhakkaru ulu al-albāb﴾ (Only the people of understanding are reminded)

He, the Exalted, says: Only those who reflect upon the proofs of God, take heed, reflect on them and ponder them, the people of intellect and sound judgment, not the people of ignorance and deficiency in intellect, are admonished by them.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "Say: O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and God's earth is spacious. Only those who are patient will be given their reward without measure" (39:10).

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say" — O Muhammad — "to My servants who believe: O My servants who believe" in God and affirm His Messenger, "fear your Lord" by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience, "for those who do good in this world there is good."

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: for those who obeyed God there is good in this world. They took "fi" (in) to be connected to "hasanah" (good), and they understood "hasanah" to mean health and well-being.

Who said this:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "For those who do good in this world there is good," he said: well-being and health.

Others said that "fi" is connected to "ahsanu" (did good), and the meaning of "hasanah" is Paradise.

* *

As for His words: "And God's earth is spacious."

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God's earth is vast and wide, so emigrate from the land of polytheism to the abode of Islam.

As narrated:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "And God's earth is spacious," he said: emigrate and withdraw from the idols.

* *

As for His words: "Only those who are patient will be given their reward without measure."

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God gives those who are patient in what they encounter in this world their reward in the Hereafter without measure, meaning: their reward is without reckoning.

Interpreters agreed with what we have said on this matter.

Who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning "Only those who are patient will be given their reward without measure," he said: No, by God, there is no measure or scale there.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "Only those who are patient will be given their reward without measure," he said: in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 15:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Say, "It is God I worship, sincerely devoted to Him in my religion. So worship what you will besides Him." Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss."﴾

He, may He be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people: "It is God I worship, sincerely devoted to Him," meaning: singling out for Him my obedience and my worship, not making for Him any partner in that. Rather, I single Him out with divinity and disassociate myself from whatever else is taken as a rival or deity. "So worship what you will" of idols and images, and other than that of what you worship from the rest of His creation, O people. You will soon know the consequence of your worship of that when you meet your Lord.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say, indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Indeed the ruined are those who cheated themselves, and whose families were destroyed along with themselves by the punishment of God, so that when they entered the Fire they had no family there, though they had families in this world.

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Say, indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾. He said: They are the disbelievers whom God created for the Fire, and created the Fire for them. The world departed from them, Paradise was forbidden to them, and God said: ﴿lost both this world and the Hereafter﴾.

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Say, indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾: These are the people of the Fire. They lost themselves in this world and lost the families, so they found in the Fire no family, though they had families in this world.

I was told from Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, he said: They cheated themselves and their families. He said: They lose their families, so they have no family to return to, and they lose themselves, so they perish in the Fire, dying while alive, and so they lose both.

As for His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Indeed the loss of these polytheists, of themselves and their families, on the Day of Resurrection, and that their destruction is the manifest loss. He, may He be exalted, says: It is the destruction which becomes clear to whoever witnesses it and knows that it is loss.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 16–18:

Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿For them there will be canopies of fire above them, and canopies below them. This is with what Allah frightens His servants. O My servants, so fear Me.﴾ (16) ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut (false deities) from worshipping them and turned back to Allah – for them is good news. So give good tidings to My servants (17) who listen to the word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.﴾ (18)

His, dhikruhu, exalted, says concerning those losers on the Day of Resurrection, in Hell: ﴿For them there will be canopies of fire above them﴾, and that is like canopies built of fire. ﴿And canopies below them﴾ means: below them is fire that rises up to them, until what rises up to them from it becomes canopies beneath them. This is like the words of His, exalted is His praise, concerning them: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them are coverings﴾, which cover them from what is beneath them in it of beds.

* *

And His words: ﴿This is with what Allah frightens His servants. O My servants, so fear Me.﴾

His, dhikruhu, says: This which I have informed you of, O people, of the punishment for the losers on the Day of Resurrection, is a warning from your Lord to you, with which He frightens you so that you will beware of it, avoid His disobedience, and repent of your disbelief by turning to belief in Him, affirming His Messenger, and following His command and prohibition, so that you may be saved from His punishment in the Hereafter. ﴿So fear Me﴾ means: fear Me by performing My obligations upon you and avoiding My disobediences, so that you may be saved from My punishment and My wrath.

* *

And His words: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut﴾

That is: they avoided worshipping everything that is worshipped besides Allah. We have already explained the meaning of the Taghut earlier, with its evidences, and mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation about it, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary here. We mentioned that in this place it means the Devil, and in this place and elsewhere it has one meaning according to us.

Mention of those who said what we have mentioned in this place:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut﴾, he said: "The Devil."

* Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping them﴾, he said: "The Devil."

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping them﴾, he said: "The Devil is here singular, and they are plural."

According to this saying of Ibn Zayd, the Taghut is a feminine singular, which is why it was said: "from worshipping them." It was also said: it was feminine because it carries the meaning of a plural.

* *

And His words: ﴿And turned back to Allah﴾

He says: they repented to Allah and returned to acknowledging His oneness, acting in His obedience, and disavowing whatever else of gods and rivals there is. The people of interpretation have spoken in a similar way to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Zayd narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And turned back to Allah﴾: "And came to Allah."

* Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿And turned back to Allah﴾, he said: "They responded to Him."

* *

And His words: ﴿For them is good news﴾

He says: for them is good news in this world of Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿So give good tidings to My servants who listen to the word﴾. His, exalted is His praise, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So give good tidings, O Muhammad, to My servants who listen to the word from those who speak it, and follow the most rightly guided and most guiding of it, and most directing to the oneness of Allah and acting in His obedience, and leave aside whatever else of speech does not indicate right guidance and does not lead to what is correct.

The people of interpretation have spoken in a similar way to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾, "and its best is obedience to Allah."

* Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾, he said: "The best of what they are commanded with, so that they act upon it."

* *

And His words: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾

His, dhikruhu, says: those who listen to the word and follow its best, those are the ones whom Allah has guided; that is, Allah has granted them success toward right guidance and reaching the correct course, not those who turn away from hearing the truth and worship what neither harms nor benefits.

* *

And His words: ﴿And those are the people of understanding﴾

That is: those possessing intellects and reason.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a known group who affirmed the oneness of Allah and disavowed the worship of everything other than Allah before the Messenger of Allah was sent, so Allah revealed this verse to His Prophet praising them.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping them ...﴾ the two verses, "My father narrated to me that these two verses were revealed concerning three men who used to say in the Jahiliyyah: 'There is no god but Allah': Zayd ibn Amr, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salman al-Farisi. Concerning them was revealed: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping them﴾ in their jahiliyyah, ﴿and turned back to Allah, for them is good news. * *

And His words: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut﴾

That is: they avoided worshipping everything that is worshipped besides Allah. We have already explained the meaning of the Taghut earlier, with its evidences, and mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation about it, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary here. We mentioned that in this place it means the Devil, and in this place and elsewhere it has one meaning according to us.

Mention of those who said what we have mentioned in this place:

According to this saying of Ibn Zayd, the Taghut is a feminine singular, which is why it was said: "from worshipping them." It was also said: it was feminine because it carries the meaning of a plural.

* *

That is: those possessing intellects and reason.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a known group who affirmed the oneness of Allah and disavowed the worship of everything other than Allah before the Messenger of Allah was sent, so Allah revealed this verse to His Prophet praising them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 16–18:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 19–20:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been justified—can you, [O Muhammad], save those who are in the Fire?﴾ ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have elevated chambers, above which are elevated chambers, with rivers flowing beneath them. [That is] the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾

By His, the Exalted's, words ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been justified﴾, He means: Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been due, in the prior knowledge of your Lord, O Muhammad, because of his disbelief in Him?

As related: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been justified﴾: "Because of his disbelief."

* *

And His words: ﴿Can you, [O Muhammad], save those who are in the Fire?﴾

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Can you, O Muhammad, save the one who is in the Fire, the one against whom the word of punishment has been justified? You would then be saving him. He dispensed with this by His words ﴿save those who are in the Fire﴾. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: This is something where a single interrogation is intended, so the interrogative is brought forward out of its proper place, and then returned to its proper place. The meaning, Allah knows best, is: Can you save those in the Fire who have had the word of punishment justified against them? He said: Similar to it, without an interrogative, is His words: ﴿Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾, where "that" is repeated twice. The meaning, Allah knows best, is: Does he promise you that you will be brought forth when you have died? Similar to it is His words: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they did not do—do not think them safe from punishment﴾. Some of them rejected the view we have related from the Basrans, and said: In His words ﴿Can you save those who are in the Fire?﴾ there is no reference back to those previously mentioned. One does not say "the people, I struck those who stood," meaning "the partitive: can you save those of them who are in the Fire?" Rather, the meaning of the phrase is: Can you, O Muhammad, guide to faith one who has already been decreed in Allah's knowledge to be among the people of the Fire, so that you save him from the Fire through faith? You are not capable of that.

* *

And His words: ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have elevated chambers﴾

He, the Exalted, says: But those who fear their Lord, by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, will have in Paradise elevated chambers, above which are elevated chambers, built high one above another, ﴿with rivers flowing beneath them﴾. He, the Exalted, means: Rivers flow beneath the trees of its gardens.

* *

And His words: ﴿[That is] the promise of Allah﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: We have promised these chambers, above which are chambers built high in Paradise, to these God-fearing people. ﴿Allah does not fail in His promise﴾. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Allah will not fail them in His promise, but He fulfils His promise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 21:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth? Then He brings forth by it crops of varying colours. Then it withers, and you see it turn yellow; then He makes it into debris. Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Do you not see﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿that Allah sends down water from the sky﴾, which is rain, ﴿and makes it flow as springs in the earth﴾. He says: He makes it run as springs in the earth. Its singular is yanbu' (spring), which is what gushes out of the earth.

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His words: ﴿and makes it flow as springs in the earth﴾, he said: every dew and water in the earth is from what was sent down from the sky.

* He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Bayan, who said: "Then He causes to grow by that water which He sent down from the sky, and made it in the earth as springs, crops ﴿of varying colours﴾", meaning: various kinds, among them wheat, barley, sesame, rice, and similar varieties ﴿Then it withers, and you see it turn yellow﴾, he says: then that crop dries up after its greenness. It is said of the land, when what is in it of greenery dries and withers: the land has "hāja" (become dry and withered), and the crop has "hāja".

* * *

As for His words: ﴿and you see it turn yellow﴾,

he says: you see it, after its greenness and moisture, has dried and become yellow, and likewise the crop when it dries it turns yellow. ﴿Then He makes it into debris﴾. Al-Hutam (debris) is the crushed fragments of straw and grass. He says: then He makes that crop, after it has become dry, into crumbled, broken fragments.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾,

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: indeed in Allah's doing that which has been described is a reminder and admonition for people of intellect and wisdom, through which they remember, and know that whoever does that is not incapable of bringing into existence whatever He wills of things, and originating whatever bodies and accidents He desires, and reviving those of His creation who have perished after their death, and restoring them after their annihilation to their former state before their annihilation, just as He did to the earth upon which He sent down water after its death, and caused to grow in it crops of varying colours by His power.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 22:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Is he whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam, so that he is upon light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Is he whom Allah has widened in heart for His knowledge, for affirming His oneness, for submitting to His lordship, and for obedience to Him, ﴿so that he is upon light from his Lord﴾ — meaning: he is upon insight into what he is upon, and certainty, through the illumination of the truth in his heart; therefore he follows the command of Allah, and refrains from what He has forbidden, in what pleases Him, like one whom Allah has hardened in heart, emptied of His remembrance, constricted from hearing the truth, following guidance, and acting rightly? The answer to the interrogative is omitted, relying on the listeners' knowledge of the intended meaning, since one of the two categories is mentioned, and in place of mentioning the other category, a statement about it is given in His words: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Is he whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam, so that he is upon light from his Lord﴾: he means the Book of Allah; he who believes in it takes from it, and to it he returns.

Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Is he whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam﴾: he said: He widened his breast for Islam, and the light: the guidance.

I was told from Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Is he whose breast Allah has expanded for Islam﴾: he said: The one whose breast is expanded is not like the one whose heart is hard.

* *

His words: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Woe to those whose hearts have become dry, who have turned away from the remembrance of Allah, meaning the Qur'an which He, may His remembrance be exalted, sent down, reminding His servants with it, but they did not believe in it, nor did they affirm what is in it. It was said: ﴿against the remembrance of Allah﴾ means "from the remembrance of Allah," so "min" was placed in the position of " 'an," as one says in speech: "I became overfull (atkhamtu) from food I ate," and "'an food I ate" have the same meaning.

* *

His words: ﴿Those are in manifest error﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: These, whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah, are in manifest error, for whoever contemplates and reflects on it with understanding will know that they are in error, deviating from the truth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 23:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book consistent within itself, oft-repeated; the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills. And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Consistent within itself﴾ means: its parts resemble one another, with no contradiction or conflict in it.

As it was reported:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book consistent within itself﴾: a verse resembles a verse, and a letter resembles a letter.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿a Book consistent within itself﴾: he said: "Mutashabih" means: some of it resembles other parts of it.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words: ﴿a Book consistent within itself﴾: he said: some of it resembles other parts of it, confirms other parts of it, and points to other parts of it.

* * *

And His words: ﴿oft-repeated﴾ (mathani).

It means: within it, reports, news, decrees, rulings and proofs are repeated.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book consistent within itself, oft-repeated﴾: he said: Allah repeated the decree in it; a surah contains a verse that resembles a verse in another surah. He was asked about it, and Ikrimah [[In al-Durr: and Ikrimah was asked about it, and he said: Allah repeated the decree in it.]].

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿a Book consistent within itself, oft-repeated﴾: he said: in the whole Qur'an.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿oft-repeated﴾: he said: Allah repeated in it the obligations, the decrees, and the prescribed punishments.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿oft-repeated﴾: he said: the Book of Allah is oft-repeated; the command is repeated in it many times.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿oft-repeated﴾: he said: the Book of Allah is oft-repeated; the command is repeated in it many times.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿oft-repeated﴾: he said: it is repeated in more than one place.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿oft-repeated﴾: it is repeated; Musa was repeated in the Qur'an, and Salih, Hud and the prophets are repeated in many places.

* * *

And His words: ﴿the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it﴾

He, the Exalted, says: the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from hearing it when it is recited to them, ﴿then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: to acting upon what is in the Book of Allah and affirming it.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because his Companions asked him to narrate to them.

The narration concerning this:

* Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Amr al-Mula'i, from Ibn Abbas, who said: They said, "O Messenger of Allah, would you not narrate to us?" He said: then it was revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech﴾.

﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills﴾. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the manner of this misguided person shielding his face from the terrible punishment. Some of them said: it is that he is thrown into Hell face-down, and that is his "shielding" himself from it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 29:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two alike in comparison? Praise belongs to God, but most of them do not know.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: God presents an example for the disbeliever in God who worships many gods and obeys a group of devils, and for the believer who worships none but the One God. He, the Exalted, says: God has struck an example for this disbeliever: a man in whom there are partners. That is, he is among a group of owners who are mutashakisun (at odds with one another), meaning disagreeing and quarrelling, bad of character, from their saying "rajul shakis" when a man is bad-tempered. Each one of them employs him according to the share and ownership he has in him. And "a man belonging wholly to one man," he says: "a man sincerely devoted to one man," meaning the believer who professes the Oneness of God and sincerely devotes his worship to God, worshipping no other and submitting to nothing else as Lord.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿wa-rajulan salaman﴾. Some readers of Makkah and Basra recited it as "wa-rajulan saliman" (a man wholly sound/sincere) and interpreted it to mean: a man sincerely devoted to a man. This has also been transmitted from Ibn Abbas.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Humayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas that he recited it: "saliman li-rajulin" with alif, and said: "There is no share in it for anyone."

The majority of readers of Madinah and Kufa recited: ﴿wa-rajulan salaman li-rajulin⦄ meaning: peace (salaman, i.e. settled/peaceful). [[The speaker of this is Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (Cairo University microfilm no. 26390, folio 159).]]

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known recitations, each recited by scholars among the readers, and their meanings are close. Whichever one the reader recites is correct. This is because salam is a verbal noun from the saying of one who says: "salima fulan lillah salaman" (meaning: he became wholly devoted to God), meaning: he became sincerely his. The Arabs say: "rabiha fulan fi tijaratihi ribhan wa-rabahan" (he profited in his trade), and "salima silman wa-salaman wa-salamah." The salim is an attribute of the man, and salam is a verbal noun from that. As for what those who prefer reciting it as salaman have supposed, that its meaning is peace (sulh), there is no sense of peace in this context, because what preceded describes the second man only in terms of the partnership of a group in him, not in terms of fighting him with anything. So it is necessary that the report about his opposite be about his being wholly devoted to one who has no partner, and there is no place for a report about war or peace in this context.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "a man in whom are partners at odds, and a man salim to a man," he said: "This is the example of the god of falsehood and the God of truth."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners at odds﴾, he said: "This is the polytheist, whom the devils pull in different directions; some of them do not acknowledge him to the others." "And a man salim to a man," he said: "This is the believer who sincerely devoted the call and the worship."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners at odds﴾ up to His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾, he said: "The partners at odds: the man who worships many gods, each group worshipping a god it is pleased with and disbelieving in what is other than it among the gods. So God struck this example for them, and struck for Himself an example, saying: 'a man belonging to a man,' meaning: they worship one God, about whom they do not differ."

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners at odds﴾, he said: "It is an example of their idols which they worshipped."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners at odds, and a man belonging wholly to one man﴾, he said: "Have you seen the man in whom are partners, all of them bad of character, none of whom is without someone taking hold of a portion of his property to employ him, while the one who owns him alone... This is only an example God struck for those who worship idols and assigned to them rights over their necks, so God struck it as an example for them, and for the one who worships Him alone (﴿Are the two alike in comparison? Praise belongs to God, but most of them do not know﴾)." And concerning His saying: "a man salim to a man," he said: "there is no shirk with him."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Are the two alike in comparison?﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Is the likeness of this man who serves a group of partners of bad character, who differ over him, in his service, while disputing with his partners over him, equal to the man who serves one who does not dispute him with any disputant? When he obeys him, he recognises the place of his obedience and honours him; and when he errs, he pardons his error. He says: Which of these two is better in condition, more at rest in body, and less in weariness and toil?

As narrated:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿Are the two alike in comparison? Praise belongs to God, but most of them do not know﴾: He says: Is one about whom there is disagreement better, or one about whom there is no disagreement?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Praise belongs to God﴾

He says: complete thanks and perfect praise belong to God alone, apart from every other object of worship.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: This shared man and the one whose ownership is singular to one are not equal; but most of these polytheists who associate others with God do not know that the two are not equal, and through their ignorance of this they worship many gods besides God. It was said: ﴿Are the two alike in comparison?﴾ and not "two alike," because both of them are struck as one example, so the word "example" was used in the singular, as He, may His praise be exalted, says: ﴿And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign﴾, since their meaning was one within the verse.

And God knows best.

On the interpretation of His words, "Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute" (39:30–31):

Allah, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed you, O Muhammad, will die after a little while, and indeed these people who deny you from your people, both believers and others among them, will die. "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute" means: then indeed all of you, believers and disbelievers, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute, so that He takes for the wronged among you from the wrongdoer, and judges between all of you with truth.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: it refers to the dispute between believers and disbelievers, and the dispute of the wronged and the wrongdoer.

Those who said this:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute," he said: the truthful will dispute with the liar, the wronged with the wrongdoer, the guided with the misguided, and the weak with the arrogant.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute," he said: the people of Islam and the people of disbelief.

Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Darawardi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib ibn al-Zubayr, who said: When this verse was revealed, "Indeed you will die, and indeed they will die. Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute," al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, will what was between us in the world, along with the particular sins, be disputed against us? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes, until every rightful claim is given its right."

Others said: rather, it refers to the dispute among the people of Islam.

Those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, from Ibn Umar, who said: This verse was revealed to us and we did not know its interpretation until the strife (al-fitna) occurred, and we said: this is what our Lord promised us, that we would dispute over "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: IbnUlayya narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Ibrahim, who said: When it was revealed, "Indeed you will die, and indeed they will die. Then indeed..." to the end of the verse, they said: What dispute is there between us, while we are brothers? He said: When Uthman ibn Affan was killed, they said: this is our dispute among ourselves.

I was told, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliya, regarding His words, "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute," he said: they are the people of the qibla.

The most correct of these opinions is that it should be said: what is meant is: indeed you, O Muhammad, will die, and indeed you, O people, will die, then indeed all of you, O people, will dispute before your Lord, believers and disbelievers, the right-doers and the wrongdoers, the oppressors and the oppressed, until each of you is given his right from the one who wronged him.

We said this is the most correct opinion because Allah, by His words, "Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute," addressed all His servants generally, and did not single out some of them over others. So it remains on its generality, as Allah made it general, and a verse may be revealed concerning one matter, and then everything that is in the same meaning as what it was revealed about falls under its ruling.

And regarding His words, "Who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him" (39:32):

Allah, may He be remembered, says: Who among the creation of Allah is greater in falsehood than one who lies against Allah, claiming that He has a son and a consort, or that He has forbidden food which He did not forbid? "And denies the truth when it comes to him" means: and denies the Book of Allah when He sent it down to Muhammad, and sent him as a messenger with it, and denies the statement "There is no god but Allah."

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding "And denies the truth when it comes to him," that it means: the Qur'an.

And regarding His words, "Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?" (39:32):

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: Is there not in the Fire a dwelling and abode for one who disbelieved in Allah and refused to affirm Muhammad (ﷺ) and follow him in what he calls to of monotheism and the judgment of the Qur'an, which he brought from Allah?

As for His saying ﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him﴾:

Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): These polytheists frighten you, O Muhammad, with those other than God, that is, the idols and gods, lest they inflict harm upon you because of your disavowal of them and your reviling of them, whereas God is sufficient for you against that.

The interpreters have said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said this:

From Yaqut's Mu'jam.] to break al-ʿUzza. Her attendant (sādin), who was her keeper, said: 'O Khalid, I warn you about her: she has a fierceness before which nothing can stand.' Khalid went to her with an axe and smashed her nose."
