Almighty God says: And whoever God forsakes, so that He leaves him astray from the path of truth and the way of right guidance, then he has no guide other than Him, no one who directs him or sets him firmly on the path of truth, or grants him success in faith in God, in affirming His Messenger, and in acting in obedience to Him. ﴿And whoever God guides, for him there is no misleader﴾ means: whoever God grants success in faith in Him and in acting by His Book, for him there is no misleader; that is, for him there is no one who will turn him aside from the truth in which he stands towards apostasy into disbelief. ﴿Is not God Mighty, Possessor of Retribution?﴾ Almighty God says: Is not God, O Muhammad, Mighty in His retribution upon the disbelievers among His creatures, Possessor of retribution against His enemies who deny His oneness?

**Commentary on the words of the Exalted: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended me some harm, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended me some mercy, could they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah. In Him the reliant should rely."﴾ (39:38)**

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And if you asked these polytheists, who associate idols and images with Allah, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah created them.' When they say that, then say: 'Have you considered, O people, these things you worship besides Allah, the idols and deities, ﴿if Allah intends harm for me﴾,' meaning, a hardship in my livelihood, ﴿'can they remove His harm from me?'﴾ meaning, can they remove from me what my Lord has afflicted me with of harm? ﴿'Or if He intends me mercy'﴾ meaning, if He intends for me mercy, that He grant me abundance in my livelihood, many possessions, ease and health in my body, ﴿'can they withhold from me what He intends to afflict me with of that mercy?'﴾"

The answer is omitted because the listener already knows it, and what has appeared in the speech points to it. The meaning is: they will say, "No." So say: "Sufficient for me is Allah, above all other things. It is He whom I worship, and it is to Him that I turn for refuge in my affairs, not to any other thing, for He is the One who suffices, and in His hand are harm and benefit, not to the idols and images, which neither harm nor benefit." ﴿In Him the reliant should rely﴾ means: whoever is a reliant should rely upon Allah, and should trust in Him alone, not in anyone else.

Those who engage in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

**Those who said so:**

Bishr said: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ up to ﴿can they remove His harm﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿or if He intends me mercy, can they withhold His mercy?﴾

The readers (qurra') differed concerning the recitation (qira'ah) of ﴿kashifatu durrihi﴾ and ﴿mumsikatu rahmatihi﴾. Some of them read them with the construct form (idafah), giving the words "harm" and "mercy" the genitive case. Others, among the readers of Madinah and most of the readers of Basrah, read them with tanwin (nunation) and gave "harm" and "mercy" the accusative case.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known recitations, close in meaning. Whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. This is like His words ﴿the plot of the disbelievers﴾ in both the construct and the nunated forms.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided, it is for [the benefit of] his own soul; and whoever strays, only against it does he stray. And you are not over them a manager.﴾

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿It is Allah who takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. His, may He be remembered, words mean: Among the proofs that divinity belongs exclusively to Allah, the One, the Subduer, to the exclusion of everything else, is that He causes death and gives life, and does whatever He wills, and nothing other than Him has power over that. So He made this a report by which He alerts them to the greatness of His power, and said: ﴿It is Allah who takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, that is, He seizes them at the end of their term and the completion of the period of their lives. He also takes the one that has not died during its sleep, just as He takes the one that has died at its death. ﴿Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death﴾. He mentioned that the spirits of the living and of the dead meet in sleep, and they become acquainted with one another as much as Allah wills. When He wills all of them to return to their bodies, Allah keeps the spirits of the dead with Him and holds them back, and sends the spirits of the living back until they return to their bodies, ﴿until an appointed term﴾, which is until the completion of the period of their lives.

His, may He be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Do you take these gods as intercessors, as you claim, even though they have no power to benefit or harm you and do not understand anything? Say to them: If you worship them for that reason, and they intercede for you with Allah, then devote your worship to Allah and single Him out with divinity, for all intercession belongs to Him. So worship the Owner who possesses the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who is able to benefit you and harm you in this world, and at your return to Him after your death, for to Him you will be returned.

By His words ﴿recoil (ishma'azzat)﴾ He means: they recoil from the Oneness of Allah. ﴿And when those others besides Him are mentioned﴾ means: when the gods they invoke besides Allah are mentioned alongside Allah, and it is said, "Those are the exalted cranes (al-gharaniq al-ula), and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for," then those who do not believe in the Hereafter rejoice at that and are delighted.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Rather, it is a trial﴾: meaning, a tribulation.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those before them said it, but what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ (50) ﴿So the evil consequences of what they earned struck them. And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evil consequences of what they earned, and they cannot escape﴾ (51)

Say: God, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, this statement was made, meaning their saying concerning God's blessing which He bestowed upon them while they were polytheists: "We have been given it on knowledge with us." ﴿Those before them﴾ means those before the polytheists of Quraysh among the bygone nations toward their messengers, out of their denial of them and their mockery of them. His saying: ﴿but what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ means: what they used to earn of deeds, which was their worship of idols, did not avail them when the punishment of God came upon them for their denial of God's messengers and their mockery of them. That is to say: their service of those idols did not benefit them, and their gods did not intercede for them with God at that time, but rather they abandoned them and disowned them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So the evil consequences of what they earned struck them﴾

That is: the evil consequences of what they earned of deeds struck those from the bygone nations who made this statement, and they were hastened to disgrace in the life of this world. This is like Qarun, who said when he was admonished: ﴿I was only given it on knowledge with me﴾, so God caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling, ﴿and he had no company to help him against God, nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾. God, whose praise is exalted, says: ﴿And those who wronged among these﴾, meaning, He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And those among your people, O Muhammad, who disbelieved in God and wronged themselves and made this statement, the evil consequences of what they earned will strike them too, just as it struck those before them for their saying it. ﴿And they cannot escape﴾ means: they will not escape their Lord nor outrun Him by fleeing in the earth from His punishment when it descends upon them; rather, it will strike them ﴿as the way of God with those who passed away before, and you will not find any change in the way of God﴾. So He did that to them, and He brought down His disgrace upon them in the hasty part of the worldly life, killing them by the sword on the day of Badr.

And those of the people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said regarding that.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, those before them said it﴾: the past nations. ﴿And those who wronged﴾ among these: he said, from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [39:52].

Says the Exalted, His remembrance: Do they not know, O Muhammad, these who We removed their harm from, so they said: "We were only given it on knowledge from us" [39:49], that hardship and ease, expansion and constriction, and trial are in the hand of Allah alone, to the exclusion of everyone other than Him; He extends provision for whom He wills, so He widens it for him, and He restricts it for whomever of His servants He wills, so He constricts it for him; and that this is among the proofs of Allah over His servants, so that they may take heed from it and be mindful, and know that turning to Him and fearing Him is to the exclusion of the deities and rivals. ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ means: indeed in Allah's extending provision for whom He wills and restricting it for whomever He wishes are signs, meaning: indications and evidences ﴿for a people who believe﴾, meaning: who affirm the truth, so they acknowledge it when they have made it clear to themselves and known its reality, that the One who does that is Allah alone, to the exclusion of everything else.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (39:53)

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about those to whom this verse refers. Some said: it refers to a group of the people of polytheism (shirk). They said, when they were called to faith in Allah: "How can we believe when we have associated partners with Allah, committed adultery, and killed a soul which Allah has forbidden, and Allah promises the doer of that the Fire? What benefit is faith to us, with what has already passed from us?" So this verse was revealed.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related: my father told me, from my paternal uncle, from my father, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾. That is because the people of Makkah said: "Muhammad claims that whoever worshipped idols and called upon another god alongside Allah, and killed a soul which Allah has forbidden, is not forgiven. So how can we emigrate and submit, when we have worshipped the gods, killed a soul which Allah has forbidden, and we are people of polytheism?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾, meaning: do not despair of My mercy; indeed Allah forgives all sins. And He said: ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him﴾. Allah only admonishes the people of understanding, and the lawful and unlawful are only for the people of faith. So it is to them that He addresses the admonition and the command: if one of them transgresses against himself, he should not despair of the mercy of Allah, and he should turn back in repentance and not delay in repenting from that transgression and the sin he committed. Allah has also mentioned in Surah Al 'Imran the believers when they asked Allah for forgiveness, and they said: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, and make firm our feet﴾. So it should be known that they used to commit excess, and He commanded them to repent from their excess.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Those who have transgressed against themselves﴾. He said: the killing of a soul in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam).

Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from some of his companions, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: These three verses were revealed in Madinah concerning Wahshi [[He is Wahshi ibn Harb al-Habashi, freedman of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, and he is the killer of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib at the Battle of Uhud. He was a dissolute man who drank wine, then later embraced Islam. (See Khulasat al-Khazraji.)]] and his companions: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ up to His saying: ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾.

Yunus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said, concerning His words: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾: "It is only for the polytheists."

Bishr told us: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ until ﴿all sins﴾. He said: It was mentioned to us that some people committed great sins in the Jahiliyyah, and when Islam came they feared that repentance would not be accepted from them, so Allah called them with this verse: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾.

Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾. He said: These are the polytheists of the people of Makkah. They said: "How can we respond to you while you claim that whoever committed adultery, or killed, or associated partners with the Most Merciful, is destined for the people of the Fire?" "Indeed, we have done all these deeds." So this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾.

Yunus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ ... the verse. He said: There was a people who were despised among the people of the Jahiliyyah. When Allah sent His Prophet, they said: "If we came to Muhammad ﷺ, we would believe in him and follow him." Some of them said to others: "How will Allah and His Messenger accept you into their religion?" They said: "Shall we not send a man to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" When they sent (a man), the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿so that I would be among the doers of good﴾.

Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Shutayr ibn Shakl and Masruq were sitting together. Shutayr said: "Either you relate what you heard from Ibn Mas'ud and I will confirm it, or I will relate and you confirm it." Masruq said: "No, rather you relate and I will confirm it." So he said: "I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: The greatest verse of hope in the Qur'an is ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾." Masruq said: "You have spoken the truth."

Others said: Rather, it refers to the people of Islam. They said: the meaning of the speech is: "Indeed Allah forgives all sins for whomever He wills." They said: It is also thus in the codex (mushaf) of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud). They said: This verse was only revealed concerning a people whom the polytheists prevented from emigrating and tormented, so they feared that there would be no repentance for them.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi told us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar said: "We used to say: there is no repentance for the one who was tempted (into apostasy)." And they used to say: "Allah will not accept anything from us. We abandoned Islam by a trial that afflicted us after we had known it." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ ... the verse. 'Umar said: "I wrote it with my own hand, then sent it to Hisham ibn al-'As." Hisham said: "When it came to me I began to read it and did not understand it, then it occurred to my mind that it was revealed about us, because of what we used to say. So I mounted my camel and joined (the Prophet) in Madinah."

Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "These verses were only revealed concerning 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and a group of the Muslims who had embraced Islam, then were tried and tortured, so they succumbed to trial. We used to say: Allah will not accept from these any repentance (sarf) or ransom ('adl) ever, a people who embraced Islam then abandoned their religion because of a punishment they were subjected to." So these verses were revealed. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was a scribe, so he wrote them with his own hand, then sent them to 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah and al-Walid ibn al-Walid and those people. So they embraced Islam and emigrated.

Ya'qub related to me: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, saying: Yunus told us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Which verse in the Qur'an is the most expansive (in hope)?" They began to mention verses of the Qur'an: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and similar ones. 'Ali said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an more expansive than: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

Abu al-Sa'ib told us: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, from Abu al-Kanud, who said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) entered the mosque and found a storyteller (qass) mentioning the Fire and the shackles. He said: He came and stood over his head and said: "What is he mentioning? Are you making people despair? ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ ... the verse."

Yunus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from al-Qurazi, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾. He said: "It is for all people."

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to me, saying: Hajjaj told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah told us, from Abu Qunbul, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani say: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jala'i related to me that he heard Thawban, freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'I would not love to have the world and whatever is in it in exchange for this verse: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ ...' the verse." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what about the one who associates partners?" The Prophet ﷺ was silent, then said: "Indeed, and whoever associates partners, indeed, and whoever associates partners" (three times).

Others said: This was revealed concerning a people who used to regard the people of major sins as people of the Fire, so Allah informed them that He forgives all sins for whomever He wills.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn al-Barqi related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, saying: Abu Mu'adh al-Khurasani told us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, used to see, or say, that there was nothing of our good deeds except that it was accepted, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds﴾. When this verse was revealed we said: 'What is it that invalidates our deeds?' We said: 'The major sins and the abominations.' So whenever we saw someone who had committed any of them we said: 'He is destroyed,' until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. When this verse was revealed we refrained from speaking about it, and whenever we saw someone who had committed any of them we feared for him, and if he had not committed any of them we hoped for him."

The most correct of the sayings in this matter is the saying of the one who said: His exalted remembrance meant by this all those who transgressed against themselves among the people of faith and of polytheism, because Allah, by His words ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾, encompassed all transgressors, and did not restrict it to one transgressor over another.

If someone says: "Does Allah forgive polytheism?" It is said: Yes, if the polytheist repents from it. What is meant by His words ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ is, as we mentioned before, for whom He wills. Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it (with an exception), and Allah has excepted polytheism from it if its possessor does not repent from it. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him﴾, and forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Thus He informed that He does not forgive polytheism except after repentance, by His words: ﴿except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾. As for what is other than it, its possessor is in the will of his Lord: if He wills, He bestows favor upon him and pardons him for it, and if He wills, He is just with him and recompenses him for it.

As for His words: ﴿do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾, it means: do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah. Thus Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father told me, from my paternal uncle, from my father, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas.

We have already mentioned the narrations concerning that in what has passed, and we have explained its meaning.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾

He says: Indeed Allah conceals all sins by pardoning their people and leaving off punishing them for them when they repent from them. ﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ toward them, that He would not punish them for them after their repentance from them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 39, verses 54–55:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And turn penitently to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped﴾ (54) ﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are not aware﴾ (55)

His, may He be exalted and remembered, saying means: Turn back, O people, to your Lord in repentance, return to Him in obedience, and respond to Him in what He has called you to: His unity, the singling out of divinity for Him, and the sincere devotion of worship to Him.

As related to us:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And turn penitently to your Lord﴾: that is, turn towards your Lord.

Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And turn penitently﴾: he said, "Respond (ajibu)."

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And turn penitently to your Lord﴾: he said, "Inabah (penitent turning) is returning to obedience and desisting from what they were upon. Do you not see Him saying: ﴿turning penitently to Him and fear Him﴾."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And submit to Him﴾

He says: humble yourselves to Him in obedience and in acknowledgment of the upright religion (al-din al-hanifi), ﴿before the punishment comes upon you﴾ from Him because of your disbelief in Him.

﴿after which you will not be helped﴾: he says, then no helper will help you, so as to rescue you from His punishment that descends upon you.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, saying means: Follow, O people, what your Lord has commanded you in His revelation, and avoid what He has forbidden you in it, and that is the best of what has been sent down to us from our Lord.

If someone says: Is there anything in the Qur'an that is better than something else? It is said to him: The whole Qur'an is good, and that is not the meaning you imagine. Rather, its meaning is: Follow, of what your Lord has sent down to you, the commands, the prohibitions, the reports, the parables, the narratives, the disputation, the promises and the threats, and its best is that you obey its command and refrain from what it forbids, because the prohibition is part of what has been sent down in the Book; so if they acted upon what they were forbidden, they would be acting upon its worst. That is its meaning.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Lest a soul should say: "Alas for my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers."﴾

He, the Exalted, says: "Turn in repentance to your Lord and submit to Him," ﴿lest a soul should say﴾, with the meaning of "lest a soul should say", ﴿"Alas for my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah"﴾. This is like His saying: ﴿And He cast firmly set mountains upon the earth lest it should shake with you﴾, meaning: lest it should not shake with you. So "an" (lest), since that is its meaning, is in the accusative position.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Alas"﴾ (yā ḥasratā):

It means: to say, "O remorse!"

As Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to me, who said: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿"Alas"﴾: he said: "Remorse." The alif in His saying ﴿"Alas"﴾ is the pronoun of the speaker, and what is intended is "O my regret!" However, the Arabs convert the yā' of the first-person pronoun into an alif in invocation, so they say "yā waylatā" (O my woe!) and "yā nadamā" (O my remorse!), and they render that in the form of a call. It may also be said "yā ḥasrata ʿalā al-ʿibād" (O regret over the servants), just as one says "yā lahf" and "yā lahfan ʿalayhi" (O grief!). Al-Farrāʾ mentioned that Abū Tharwān recited to him:

﻿"You visit them, while I do not visit your women... alas for the sons of the slave-women, the firewood gatherers" [The verse is by Abū Tharwān al-ʿUklī, and it is one of al-Farrāʾ's witnesses in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān (folio 285). He said: his saying "yā ḥasratā, yā waylatā" is attached to the speaker: the Arabs change the yā' into an alif in every utterance whose meaning is invocation, and it comes out in the form of a call. And they may say "yā ḥasrah," just as they say "yā lahf ʿalā fulān" and "yā lahfā ʿalayhi." He said: Abū Tharwān al-ʿUklī recited to me: "You visit them, and I do not visit..." the verse. Thus it is in the genitive, as the one being called is put in the genitive when the speaker attaches it to himself. Those of the interpreters said what we have said concerning this.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Or [that] one should say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."﴾ (39:57) ﴿Or [that] one should say when he sees the punishment, "If only I had a return [to the world], so I would be among the doers of good."﴾ (39:58)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Turn in repentance to your Lord, O people, and submit to Him, lest any soul say on the Day of Resurrection, "Alas for me, for what I neglected concerning Allah's side," that is, regarding the command of Allah. And lest another soul say, "If only Allah had guided me to the truth and granted me success in right guidance, I would have been among those who feared Him by obeying Him and following His pleasure." Or lest another say when it sees the punishment of Allah and witnesses it, ﴿"If only I had a return,"﴾ meaning, "If only I had a return to the world," ﴿"so I would be among the doers of good,"﴾ those who did good in obeying their Lord and acting upon what the messengers had commanded them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said about this.

Regarding the parsing of His words ﴿"fa-akuna"﴾ (so I would be), there are two possibilities. One is that it is in the accusative as an answer to "law" (if only). The second is that it is in the accusative by being a continuation of the position of "karrah" (a return), with the meaning of the return being: "If only I had the chance to return," as the poet said:

"Of it you have nothing but remembrance and regret, and you ask about its riders, where they headed?"

The poem is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 286 of the University manuscript), and the evidence lies in his words "wa-tas'alu" (and you ask), since it is permissible to put it in the accusative by implying "an" (that), coordinating the verb with an explicit noun, like the statement of Maysun bint Bahdal al-Kalbiyyah, wife of Mu'awiyah: "labsa 'abā'ah wa-tuqarra 'aynī" (wearing a cloak and [that] my eye be comforted), meaning "wa-an tuqarra 'aynī." It is also permissible to make it nominative, since "an" does not appear before it. Al-Farra' said: His words "law anna li karrah fa-akuna min al-muhsinin": the accusative in "fa-akuna" is an answer to "law." And if you wish, it can be taken as coordinated with the implied "an" which you supply in "al-karrah," as they say: "law anna akurr fa-akuna" (if only I could return and be [among them]). Similar to this, what is put in the accusative by implying "an" is His words: "And it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition, or that He should send a messenger" (42:51), meaning, and Allah knows best: "it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation." Had "fa-yuhiya" been put in the nominative, since "an" does not appear before it nor with it, it would have been correct, and some reciters have read it so. Some reciters recited to me: "Fa-ma laka minha ghayra dhikra wa-hasrah," the verse. The commentary on the words of God Almighty: ﴿Yes, indeed My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers﴾ (39:59)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, refuting the speaker who said: ﴿If only God had guided me, I would have been among the God-fearing﴾, and the speaker who said: ﴿If only I had another chance, I would be among the good-doers﴾: "It is not as you say. ﴿Yes indeed, My signs came to you﴾, O you who wish from God to be returned to the world so that you might be among the good-doers. ﴿My signs﴾ means: My proofs have come to you, through a messenger I sent to you and a Book I revealed to be recited to you, containing its promise, its warning and its reminder. ﴿But you denied them﴾ and ﴿were arrogant﴾ in refusing to accept and follow them, ﴿and you were among the disbelievers﴾," meaning: you were among those who act as the disbelievers act, follow their way, and adopt their path.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 60:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened.  Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see﴾ O Muhammad, these ones ﴿who lied about Allah﴾ from your people, so they claimed that He has a son, and that He has a partner, and they worshipped gods other than Him, ﴿their faces blackened﴾. The word "faces" (wujuhuhum) is in the nominative by virtue of "blackened" (musawaddah), yet it carries the sense of the accusative, because it, together with its predicate, completes the verb "you will see." Had "blackened" (musawaddah) been placed before "faces" (wujuh), it would be in the accusative, and the accusative "blackened faces" would be governed by a verb in the speech, not in the Qur'an. When "blackened" is placed after, it is permissible, as the poet said:

Leave me, for your command will not be obeyed, and you will not find my forbearance lost. [[The verse is attributed to ʿAdi ibn Zayd, as al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 286) from the Jami'ah manuscript. It is among the verses of Sibawayh's Kitab (1:87) and is cited in Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra of al-Baghdadi (2:368). The point of citation is that his saying "forbearance" (hilmi) is a substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal) from the "ya" in "alfaytani." Ibn Jinni said in I'rab al-Hamasah: "Substitution from the first-person and second-person pronouns is permissible only when it is partial substitution or substitution of inclusion, as in your saying: 'I was amazed by you, your intellect,' and 'I struck you, your head.'" End. He said in the Khizanah: The verse was attributed by Sibawayh to a man from Khath'am or Bajilah, and Ibn al-Sarraj followed him in his Usul. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj attributed it to ʿAdi ibn Zayd al-ʿIbadi, and this is the correct view; the author of al-Hamasah al-Basriyyah also said so and cited further verses after it from the poem. End.]]

So "the forbearance" (al-hilm) and "the lost" (al-mada') are in the accusative by repetition of "alfaytani." The Arabs do the same with everything that requires a subject and a predicate, such as "zanna" (to think) and its sisters. As for "musawaddah," the Arabs have two forms: musawaddah and musawadda'. The people of the Hijaz, as reported from them, say: "qad iswadda wajhuhu" (his face became black), "ihmarra" (became red), and "ishhabba" (became grey-white). Some Basran grammarians reported from one of them that he said: the pattern "if'alla" occurs only with a single-colour adjective, such as "ashab" (grey-white). He said: it does not occur with forms like "ahmar" (red), because "ashab" is a colour that comes into being, whereas "ahmar" does not come into being.

He says: Is there not in Hell a place of abode and dwelling for those who were arrogant towards Allah, and so refused to affirm His oneness and to submit to His obedience in what He commanded and forbade?

Exalted is His remembrance says: Allah will save from Hell and its punishment those who were mindful of Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions in the world, ﴿with their triumph﴾, meaning with their success (fawz). It is the noun form (mafazah) derived from that root.

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Say: "Is it other than God that you order me to worship, you ignorant ones?" (64) And it has certainly been revealed to you, and to those before you: "If you associate partners with God, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ (65)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people, who call you to the worship of idols: ﴿Is it other than God⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ O you who are ignorant of God⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ that you order me﻿﻿﻿﻿ to worship﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿?﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ ﴾, meaning: that I should worship, when worship is fit for nothing but Him.

The grammarians (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) differed over the governing word (al-ʿamil, the word that determines the case) of the accusative in ﴿أَفَغَيْرَ﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: the sense is "Say: Is it other than God that you order me," meaning, "Is it other than God that you order me to worship?" It is as if he intended the particle to be dropped (al-ilghaʾ, treating a word as superfluous in the construction), and God knows best; as you say, "So-and-so went, [[As it stands in the original; this is unclear. al-Shawkani, in Fath al-Qadir (4:461), explains the governing word of the accusative in "ghayr" clearly and sufficiently, so refer to him. Perhaps the original phrase was: "So-and-so went, not knowing…" etc.]] he knows," treating it as meaning "so he does not know." Some grammarians of Kufa said: "ghayr" is in the accusative governed by "aʿbudu" (I worship), and "an" may be omitted and inserted, because it marks the future. Just as you say, "I want to strike" and "I want [to] strike," and "perhaps I will strike" and "perhaps [I] strike," so in its governing it demands the future, like your saying "Zayd, I will surely strike him." Therefore it is omitted, and what follows it governs what precedes it. We have no need for the idea of superfluity (al-lagw).

As for His words: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you, and to those before you﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ ﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And it has certainly been revealed to you, O Muhammad, by your Lord, and to those before you of the messengers: ﴿If you associate partners with God, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾, meaning: If you associate anything with God, O Muhammad, your deeds will be nullified, and you will gain no reward for them, and you will reach no recompense except the recompense of one who associates partners with God. This is an inverted (muʾakhkhar) construction whose meaning is one of priority. The meaning of the speech is: "It has certainly been revealed to you, 'If you associate partners, your deeds will surely be nullified and you will surely be among the losers,' and [it has been revealed] to those before you," in the sense of: "and to those messengers before you, the like of what was revealed to you about it." So beware of associating anything with God, lest you perish.

As for the meaning of His words: ﴿and you will surely be among the losers﴾, it means: you will surely be among those who perish by associating partners with God, if you associate anything with Him.

In the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone, and be among the thankful﴾ (66) ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ (67).

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not worship what these polytheists of your people have ordered you to worship, O Muhammad. Rather, worship Allah alone, apart from everything else besides Him, of gods, idols and rivals. ﴿And be among the thankful﴾ to Allah for His favour upon you, in what He has bestowed of guidance to worship Him and of disavowal of the worship of idols and images. The word "Allah" is in the accusative case by the verb ﴿fa-'budh﴾ which comes after it, because this is a resumption of speech (radd al-kalam). Had it been put in the accusative by an implied verb before it, it would have been sound and permissible, since the Arabs say: "Zayd, let him stand" (fa-l-yaqum), and "Zaydan, let him stand" (fa-l-yaqum), in the nominative and accusative. The nominative is on the basis of "let Zayd look, let him stand," and the accusative on the basis of "look at Zayd, let him stand."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Yahya related to us, he said: Fudayl ibn ʿIyad related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed in wonder and in affirmation.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, from Mansur, from Khaythama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a rabbi from the rabbis of the Jews came to him, sat with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Tell us." He said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, blessed and exalted, will place the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, the water and the trees on one finger, and all creatures on one finger, then He will shake them and say: I am the King. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, affirming what he said, then he recited this verse: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ ... the verse.

Muhammad related to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, similarly.

Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar and ʿAbbas ibn Abi Talib related to me, they said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt related to us, he said: Abu Kudayna related to us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: A Jew passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was sitting, and said: "O Jew, tell us." He said: How do you say, O Abu al-Qasim, on the day when Allah places the heaven on this, and the earth on this, and the mountains on this, and the rest of creation on this? So Allah revealed: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ ... the verse.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, he said: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Abu al-Qasim, has it reached you that Allah carries the creatures on one finger, the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, and the moist earth on one finger? He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, and Allah revealed: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

Others said: Rather, the heavens are in His right hand and the earths in His left hand.

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAli ibn Dawud related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Hazim informed us, he said: Abu Hazim related to me, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Miqsam, that he heard ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar say: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the pulpit saying: "The Almighty will take His heavens and His earth in His two hands." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) clenched his hands, and began to clench and open them, then he said: "I am the Merciful, I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) swayed to his right and to his left, so much so that I saw the pulpit move from its lowest part, so much so that I said: Will it fall with the Messenger of Allah?

Abu ʿAlqama al-Farawi ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad related to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Nafiʿ related to me, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Almighty will take His heavens and His earth in His two hands," and he clenched his hand and began to clench and open it, then said: "I am the Almighty, I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) swayed to his right and to his left, so much so that I saw the pulpit move from its lowest part, so much so that I said: Will it fall with the Messenger of Allah?

Al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAyyash al-Himsi related to me, he said: Bishr ibn Shuʿayb related to us, he said: My father informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab related to us, he said: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abu Hurayra, that he used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold up the heavens in His right hand, then He will say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"

It was reported to me from Harmala ibn Yahya, he said: Idris ibn Yahya al-Qaʾid related to us, he said: Hayawa informed us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Nafiʿ, the freedman of Ibn ʿUmar, informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection in His hand, and fold up the sky in His right hand, and say: I am the King."

Muhammad ibn ʿAwn related to me, he said: Abu al-Mughira related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, he said: Saʿid ibn Thawban al-Kala'i related to us, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: A rabbi from the Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: Have you considered when Allah says in His Book: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾, then where will the creatures be at that time? He said: "They will be in it like the writing on a book."

Ibrahim ibn Saʿid al-Jawhari related to us, he said: Abu Usama related to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Hamza related to us, he said: Salim related to me, from his father, that he informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will fold up the heavens and take them in His right hand, and fold up the earth and take it in His left hand, then He will say: I am the King; where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?"

It has been said: This verse was revealed because of a Jew who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the attributes of the Lord.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salama related to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from Muhammad, from Saʿid, who said: A group of Jews came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Muhammad, this Allah created creation; then who created Him? The Prophet (ﷺ) became so angry that his color changed, then he was overcome with anger for his Lord. Gabriel came to him and calmed him, and said: Lower your wing, O Muhammad. And there came to him from Allah an answer to what they had asked about. He said: Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent﴾. When the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to them, they said: Describe for us your Lord, how is His creation, how is His arm, how is His forearm? The Prophet (ﷺ) became angrier than his first anger, then he was overcome, and Gabriel came and said the same as before, and brought him the answer to what they had asked: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yaʿqub related to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, who said: The Jews spoke about the attributes of the Lord, saying what they did not know and had not seen. So Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾, then He explained to people His greatness, saying: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾, and so He made their description of Allah with which they described Him a form of shirk.

Some grammarians of Basra said: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ speaks of His power, similar to His words: ﴿or what your right hands possess﴾, meaning: what you had power over. The sovereignty is not attributed to the right hand alone, to the exclusion of the rest of the body. He said: His words "handful" are like your saying to a man: this is in your hand and in your grasp. The reports we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his Companions and others bear witness to the soundness of this view.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Harun ibn al-Mughira related to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Habib ibn Abi ʿAmra, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAʾisha, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His words: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾, "Where will people be on that day?" He said: "On the Bridge (al-Sirat)."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾

He, the Exalted, says, declaring Allah far above and free of what these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, associate with Him, those who say to you: Worship the idols besides Allah, and prostrate to our gods.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 68:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: "And Israfil will blow into the Horn." We have already explained the meaning of al-Sur (the Trumpet) earlier, with its supporting evidence, and mentioned the disagreement of the scholars concerning it, and the correct view with its evidence, so that is sufficient and there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

His saying ﴿and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead﴾

He says: "They will die, and that is at the first blast."

As related:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead﴾: He said: "They will die."

* *

His saying: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾

The people of interpretation differed about who is meant by the exception in this verse. Some of them said it refers to Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael), Israfil, and Malik al-Mawt (the Angel of Death).

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾: He said: Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil and Malik al-Mawt.

⁕ Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, who said: al-Fadl ibn Isa narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾. It was said: "Who are those whom Allah has excepted, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Jibril, Mika'il and Malik al-Mawt. When he takes the souls of the creatures, he will say: 'O Malik al-Mawt, who remains?' And He knows best. He will say: 'Glory be to You, blessed are You, my Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour. Jibril, Mika'il and Malik al-Mawt remain.' He will say: 'O Malik al-Mawt, take the soul of Mika'il.' So he will fall like a great mountain. Then He will say: 'O Malik al-Mawt, who remains?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour. Jibril and Malik al-Mawt remain.' He will say: 'O Malik al-Mawt, die.' So he will die. Then He will say: 'O Jibril, who remains?' Jibril will say: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour. Jibril remains, and he is in the position that he holds from Allah.' He will say: 'O Jibril, there must be a death.' So he will fall prostrate, flapping his wings, saying: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour. You are the Everlasting, and Jibril is the dying, the perishing.' He will take his soul in the ring from which he was created. Then it will fall upon Mika'il that the excellence of His creation over the creation of Mika'il is like the excellence of a great mountain over the small hills (al-zirab)." [Note in the text: In al-Lisan, al-zarb: a spread-out mountain. It is said it is a small mountain, and it is said the small hills. Its plural is zirab.]

Others said: The exception refers to the martyrs.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Umarah, from Dhu Hujr al-Yahmadi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿fell dead, except whom Allah wills﴾: He said: "The martyrs, a circle around the Throne of Allah, wearing swords across their shoulders."

Others said: The exception in the terror refers to the martyrs, and in the falling dead to Jibril, the Angel of Death, and the bearers of the Throne.

Mention of those who said that, and the report that came from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning it:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: al-Muharibi Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Trumpet will be blown three blasts: the first is the blast of terror (fazaʿ), the second is the blast of falling dead (sa'q), and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the Worlds, blessed and exalted. Allah will command Israfil with the first blast, and he will say: 'Blow the blast of terror.' The people of the heavens and the people of the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills." Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is excepted when He says: ﴿so they were terrified, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom Allah wills﴾?" He said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror reaches only the living. Those are alive with their Lord, being provided for. Allah protects them from the terror of that day and secures them. Then Allah will command Israfil with the blast of falling dead, and he will say: 'Blow the blast of falling dead.' The people of the heavens and the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills, and they will be motionless. Then the Angel of Death will come to the Mighty, blessed and exalted, and say: 'O Lord, the people of the heavens and earth have died, except whom You wish.' He will say to him, and He knows best: 'Who remains?' He will say: 'You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and Jibril and Mika'il remain.' Allah will say to him: 'Be silent. I have decreed death upon whoever is beneath My Throne.' Then the Angel of Death will come and say: 'O Lord, Jibril and Mika'il have died.' Allah will say, and He knows best: 'Who remains?' He will say: 'You remain, the Living who does not die, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain.' Allah will say: 'Let the bearers of the Throne die,' and they will die. Allah the Exalted will command the Throne, and it will seize the Trumpet. Then it will say: 'O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died.' He will say: 'Who remains?' and He knows best. It will say: 'You remain, the Living who does not die, and I remain.' He will say: 'You are of My creation; I created you for what I saw. So die, you will not live again.' So it dies."

This report related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more worthy of being sound, because the falling dead (sa'qah) in this context means death. As for the martyrs, although they are alive with Allah as Allah the Exalted has informed, they had already tasted death before that.

Allah, may His praise be exalted, meant by the exception in this place the exception from those who fell dead at the blast of falling dead, not from those who had died long before that, a long time and age earlier. For if it were permissible that what is meant were those who had perished and tasted death before the time of the blast of falling dead, it would have to be that what is meant were those who had perished and tasted death before that, since they would be among those who do not fall dead at that time, if the dead person does not undergo another death in that state.

Others said regarding this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿fell dead, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom Allah wills﴾. Al-Hasan said: "Allah makes the exception, and He does not leave any one of the people of the heavens or the people of the earth without making them taste death?" Qatadah said: "Allah has made the exception, and Allah knows best to what its exception has come." He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah said: "An angel came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, choose to be a prophet-king or a prophet-servant.' He gestured to me to be humble, so I said: 'A prophet-servant.' Then I was given two qualities: I was made the first whom the earth splits open for, and the first intercessor. I raise my head and find Musa holding the Throne. Allah knows best whether he fell dead after the first falling or not."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Ubaydah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, who said: Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Jew in the market of Madinah said: "By the One who chose Musa above mankind." A man of the Ansar raised his hand and slapped his face, saying: "Do you say this while the Messenger of Allah is among us?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.﴾ I will be the first to raise his head, and there is Musa grasping one of the legs of the Throne. I do not know whether he raised his head before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata, from al-Hasan, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is as if I am shaking the dust from my head, the first to come out. I turn and see no one except Musa clinging to the Throne. I do not know whether he is among those whom Allah excepted from the blast, or whether he was raised before me."

* *

His saying: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on﴾

He, the Exalted, says: "Then the Trumpet will be blown another blast," and the pronoun in "fihi" (in it) refers to the Trumpet.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾: He said: "In the Trumpet, and it is the blast of resurrection."

It is mentioned that between the two blasts is forty years.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: "Between the two blasts is forty." They said: "O Abu Hurayrah, forty days?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." "Then Allah will send down water from the sky, and you will sprout as the herb sprouts, and nothing of the human being will decay except one bone, which is the coccyx, and from it the creation will be reassembled on the Day of Resurrection."

⁕ Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: al-Balkhi ibn Iyas narrated to us, who said: I heard Ikrimah say regarding His saying ﴿fell dead, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth﴾... the verse: "The first is from the world, and the last is from the Hereafter."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on﴾: He said: The Prophet of Allah said: "Between the two blasts is forty." His companions said: "We did not ask him about that, nor did he add anything to it, except that they used to think by their own opinion that it was forty years."

It was mentioned to us that in those forty there will be a rain called the rain of life, until the earth becomes good and stirs, and the bodies of people grow like herbs. Then the second blast will be blown: ﴿and at once they will be standing, looking on﴾. He said: It was mentioned to us that Mu'adh ibn Jabal asked the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): "How will the believers be raised on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "They will be raised naked, uncircumcised, with kohl in their eyes, at the age of thirty years."

* *

His saying: ﴿and at once they will be standing, looking on﴾

He says: "Then at once, those who fell dead at the previous blast and others of all of Allah's creation who had been dead before that will be standing, up from their graves and places on the earth, alive as they were before their death, looking at the command of Allah concerning them."

As related:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and at once they will be standing, looking on﴾: He said: "When they are resurrected."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 69:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: "So the earth will light up with the light of its Lord." It is said: "The sun shone (ashraqat al-shams)" when it became clear and bright, and "it rose (ashraqat)" when it came up. This happens when the Most Merciful appears to decide the judgment between His creatures.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾ He said: "They will not be harmed by its light, except as one is not harmed by the sun on a clear day without haze."

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾ He said: "It lit up."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and the Book will be placed﴾:

That is, the book of their deeds, for their reckoning and recompense.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the Book will be placed﴾ He said: "The books of their deeds."

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and the Book will be placed﴾ He said: "The reckoning."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾

It means: the prophets will be brought so that their Lord may question them about what their nations answered them with and how they responded to them in the world, when the message of Allah came to them. And "the witnesses" means: the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), whom their Lord will call as witnesses against the Messengers concerning their conveying the message of Allah with which their Lord sent them to their nations, when their nations denied that they had conveyed the message of Allah to them. "Shuhada'" is the plural of "shahid" (witness). This is similar to the saying of Allah: ﴿And thus We have made you a median community that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾. It has been said that by His saying ﴿the witnesses﴾ is meant those who were killed in the way of Allah. But what they said in this regard has no great meaning in this context, because it follows His saying ﴿and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought and judgment will be given between them with truth﴾. This is clear evidence for the correctness of what we have said: that the prophets and the witnesses are summoned only for the judgment between the prophets and their nations, and that "shuhada'" is the plural of "shahid," those who testify for the prophets against their nations, as we have mentioned.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾: "They will testify for the Messengers that they conveyed the message, and to the nations' denial of them."

Mention of those who said the other view we have related:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾: "Those who were martyred in obedience to Allah."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and judgment will be given between them with truth﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: judgment will be given between the prophets and their nations with truth, and His judgment between them with truth is that no one is burdened with the sin of another, and no soul is punished except for what it has earned.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do﴾ (70). ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: "Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has come due against the disbelievers"﴾ (71).

He, dhikruhu (exalted is His remembrance), says: And Allah will then pay every soul in full the recompense of its deeds, whether good or evil. He is most knowing of what they did in the world of obedience or disobedience, and nothing of that escapes His knowledge. He will recompense them for it on the Day of Resurrection, so He rewards the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for what he did wrong.

* *

His words: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell﴾

He says: He will gather those who disbelieved in Allah to His Fire, which He has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection, in companies, group by group and party by party.

As related:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿in groups﴾: he said: "Companies."

* *

His words: ﴿until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And has caused us to inherit the earth﴾: "The land of the Garden," and he recited: ﴿That the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We may settle in the Garden wherever we will﴾:

He says: we take a dwelling from the Garden, and dwell in it wherever we love and desire.

As:

⁕ Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿We may settle in the Garden wherever we will﴾: "We will descend from it wherever we will."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So excellent is the reward of the workers﴾:

He says: so excellent is the reward of those who obey Allah and work for Him in the world, which is the Garden, for whoever Allah grants it in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 75:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [their Lord] with praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, "Praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And you see, O Muhammad, the angels encircling the Throne of the Most Merciful." By "the Throne" He means the seat (al-sarir).

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾: "encircling."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾, he said: "encircling the Throne." He said: "The Throne: the seat."

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed over the reason for the entry of "min" (from) in His saying ﴿surrounding from around the Throne﴾, the meaning being: surrounding the Throne.

And regarding His saying ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate [others with Allah], your deeds will surely be nullified﴾, some grammarians of Basra said: "min" was introduced in these two places for emphasis (tawkid), and Allah knows best, like your saying: "There came to me not anyone" (ma ja'ani min ahad). Others said: qabl (before), hawl (around), and what is similar to them are adverbs (zuruf) which "min" may enter and leave, as in: "I came to you before Zayd" and "min qabl Zayd," and "We circumambulated around you" and "min hawlika." This is not of the same kind as "ma ja'ani min ahad," because the position of "min" in their saying "ma ja'ani min ahad" is nominative (raf'), and it is a noun.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that "min" in these places, I mean in His saying ﴿min hawl al-'Arsh﴾ and "min qablika" and what is similar to that, even though it entered upon adverbs, is for emphasis.

* *

His saying: ﴿exalting [their Lord] with praise of their Lord﴾

He says: they pray around the Throne of Allah, thanking Him. The Arabs sometimes introduce the letter "ba'" (with) with tasbih (glorification) and sometimes omit it, so they say: "sabbih bi-hamd Allah" and "sabbih hamd Allah," as the Most High said: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿So glorify with the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿And it will be judged between them in truth﴾

He says: Allah judges between the prophets who were brought, and the witnesses and their nations, with justice, so He settles the people of faith in Allah and in what His messengers brought in Paradise, and the people of disbelief in Him and in what His messengers brought in the Fire. ﴿And it will be said, "Praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾: He says: the conclusion of the judgment between them is concluded with thanks to the One who originated their creation, to whom belongs divinity, and the dominion of everything in the heavens and the earth of creation, of angels, jinn and humankind, and other categories of creation.

Qatadah used to say regarding this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿exalting [their Lord] with praise of their Lord﴾ ... the verse, all of it, he said: "The first of creation was opened with praise to Allah, so He said: 'Praise is to Allah who created the heavens and the earth,' and it was concluded with praise, so He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'Praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'﴾"

End of the tafsir of Surah az-Zumar.
